title: Resumable-stream checkpoints and stale-fragment salvage with v1 client compatibility shim
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: We currently have edge cases where clients disconnect mid-generation (network drop, app crash, mobile backgrounding) and our system either holds expensive KV cache / worker state for long TTLs or aggressively GC partial outputs, causing lost-progress and poor UX for clients that try to resume. Additionally, older v1 streaming clients do not support the new resume token handshake and still rely on connection semantics that assume immediate retry will continue the same generation. This creates both waste (reserved execution slots) and user-visible failures for tool/function-calling flows that embed ephemeral tool handles in the token stream.

Goal: Implement resumable-stream checkpoints (lightweight per-session checkpoints at safe yield points), a salvage pass to reclaim and attempt to stitch salvageable partial fragments back into a resumed generation, and a small compatibility shim that detects v1 clients and offers best-effort graceful fallbacks. Ensure structured-output and in-flight function-call boundaries are preserved when salvaging.

Design proposal (high level):
- Checkpoint model: Emit checkpoint metadata every N tokens or at structured-output/function-call boundaries. Checkpoints are immutable small descriptors (generation id, sequence token idx, KV snapshot pointer, last-safe-fence flag). Stored in a compact TTL bucket keyed by customer+session.
- Soft-abort marker: When client disconnects, mark the generation as "soft-aborted" with a short grace window (configurable, default 60s) where an immediate resume attempt reattaches to the worker. After the grace window we enter "salvageable" state where the salvage service will run a deterministic prefix-scan to produce a compact prefix that can be used to resume or to synthesize a fallback response.
- Salvage algorithm: A worker-side pass that validates token continuity, verifies tool-call boundaries (function call start/end tokens), and reconstructs minimal KV-prefix state. If a function/tool was invoked but never returned, we mark the fragment as "tool-incomplete" and attach a synthetic placeholder event to the salvage metadata to be surfaced to client on resume.
- Compatibility shim: For v1 clients that don't support resume tokens, we will detect client-version header and enable a conservative behavior: extend soft-abort grace to 120s, emit an out-of-band error code that suggests client retry with resume support, and attempt an automatic short-lived warm reservation of resources to reduce cold-loss for common mobile reconnect patterns.
- Observability & safety: New metrics (partial_reclaims, salvage_success_rate, resume_latency_p50/p95, tool-incomplete_count) and structured logs for salvage decisions. Add an SLO: salvage_success_rate >= 95% for non-tool-incomplete fragments for Canary 2.

Trade-offs considered:
- TTL length vs resource cost: longer TTLs improve resume success but increase cost. We pick a small default TTL (60s soft, 15m salvage bucket) and make it customer-configurable for Dedicated/Private.
- Conservatism around function/tool boundaries: We avoid attempting to synthesize tool outputs to prevent hallucinations; instead we return explicit placeholders and developer-facing diagnostics.
- Compatibility shim complexity: We keep shim narrow to avoid long-lived protocol branches; eventual deprecation plan for v1 shim after 6 months will be published.

Rollout plan:
1) Feature flags behind runtime-1.21 canary for internal traffic (10%) with metrics enabled.
2) Run canary for two weeks, iterate on salvage heuristics.
3) Enable gradual rollout by customer tag and expose toggle in Console per-project.
4) Post-rollout: publish migration doc for SDKs explaining resume token usage and best practices.

Acceptance criteria (high-level):
- Resume handshake succeeds and reattaches to the same logical generation in >= 90% of reconnects within the soft-abort window during canary.
- Salvage service can reclaim and stitch prefixes for >= 95% of salvageable fragments without producing invalid structured outputs.
- v1 shim reduces immediate-cold-loss incidents by 60% in mobile reconnect simulation.

Risks and mitigation:
- Risk: Salvage could surface partial tool calls and confuse downstream consumers. Mitigation: Attach explicit metadata and developer-visible placeholders; do not fabricate tool outputs.
- Risk: Increased storage/coordination overhead. Mitigation: Compact checkpoint format and per-customer configurable TTLs; metrics to monitor cost.

Open questions:
- Should we offer an API endpoint to fetch salvage diagnostics for debugging? (pro: good visibility; con: additional surface area).
- For Dedicated, do we expose a longer default grace window? Suggest yes, via config.

Next steps:
- Design doc PR to /docs/runtime/resume-salvage.md (linked below).
- Prototype checkpoint metadata format and small in-memory salvage runner on dev cluster.
- Implement compatibility shim detection and conservative extension path.

2026-03-07 - Diego Alvarez: Implemented first salvage pass on dev. Found edge-case where function-call end tokens are split across segments; added stronger boundary detection and sanity checks.
2026-03-11 - Security (Nadia R.): No secrets in checkpoint metadata and pointers are ephemeral. Confirmed KMS not required for these descriptors.
